# Plan and Implement

## Change Summary

Added canonical N/C/O2 budget plumbing to `tank_core`: `TankState` now exposes canonical `total_nitrogen()`, `total_carbon()`, and `budget_totals()` helpers backed by shared stoichiometry helpers in `types/budget.rs`, and `Engine` now supports optional per-tick budget tracking via `enable_budget_tracking()` / `budget_ledger()`. When enabled, the engine records per-action and per-system N/C/O2 deltas into a `BudgetLedger`/`TickBudgetRecord` history without allocating or recording anything on the default disabled path. Added integration coverage for helper completeness, 24-tick closed-system conservation, explicit water-change export accounting, and disabled-path behavior.

## Steps

1. [Completed] Audit the existing state layout and hourly/daily systems to identify every currently modeled N-, C-, and O2-bearing pool plus the engine stages that need per-tick attribution.
2. [Completed] Implement canonical element-total helpers and shared stoichiometry utilities, then wire an optional `BudgetLedger` into `Engine` so queued actions and systems record per-stage budget deltas only when tracking is enabled.
3. [Completed] Add budget-focused integration tests covering helper completeness, 24-tick closed-system N/C conservation, explicit water-change export attribution, and the disabled tracking path.
4. [Completed] Format and validate the change set against the broader `tank_core` test suite to catch regressions beyond the new ledger coverage.

## Validation Evidence

- `cargo test -p tank_core --test budget_tracking` passed (6 tests covering canonical totals, 24-tick conservation, water-change export attribution, and disabled-path gating).
- `cargo test -p tank_core --test water_change_mass_balance` passed (8 tests), confirming the new engine instrumentation did not regress existing water-change behavior.
- `cargo test -p tank_core` passed across the full `tank_core` suite.

## Outstanding Risks

- Canonical live-biomass C/N totals still depend on shared stoichiometric helper assumptions in `types/budget.rs`; if future phases add new explicit element-bearing fields or refine biomass composition, those helpers and tests must be updated together.
- The closed-system conservation checks use a quiescent no-growth scenario. Richer gameplay states may still expose pre-existing stoichiometry gaps in systems that do not yet move every element explicitly, but the new ledger will now make those imbalances inspectable.
- The worktree also contains unrelated user changes outside this task in `crates/tank_scenarios/src/lib.rs`, `crates/tank_tui/src/main.rs`, and `.ralph-burning/`.
